catalog_quote: 3.3 節では、アクセントの体系について論じる。国頭方言は、音の相対的な高低によって語を弁別するピッチ・アクセント (pitch accent) を持つ。... 国頭方言のアクセント核はもっぱらピッチ上昇によって実現される。... 本節では、高山（2013）にならい、国頭方言は上げ核の有無と位置が弁別的な体系であると考える。 3.3.1. 概論 前述のように、国頭方言は核の有無と位置が弁別的である体系を持つ。すなわち、国頭方言の語は、核を持つもの（hagami「鏡」、futabi「今年」、guzjija「鯨」など）と持たないもの（hjibusji「煙」など）とに分類することが可能である。... 国頭方言における核の位置は、後ろから 1 モーラ目、後ろから 2 モーラ目、後ろから 3 モーラ目のいずれかである。したがって核の有無（あるかないか）と位置（後ろから 1 番目か 2 番目か 3 番目か）とに基づいて、4 種類のアクセント型が区別される。以下、国頭方言の 4 種類のアクセント型をそれぞれ a 型、b 型、c 型、d 型と呼ぶことにする。a 型は核のない型、すなわち無核であり、b 型、c 型、d 型は核のある型、すなわち有核である。... [§3.3.3] a. 核を担う韻律単位はモーラである。b. a 型は核のない型であり、b 型は後ろから 1 モーラ目に、c 型は後ろから 2 モーラ目に、d 型は後ろから 3 モーラ目に核がある型である。ただし b 型は 2 モーラ以上の助詞が後接するとき、核の位置が 1 モーラ右側に移る。c. 核は上げ核であり、核があるモーラの次の韻律単位を上昇させる。

Words lacking a kernel are unaccented (Type A), whereas words with a kernel are accented. ... In Type C words, the kernel is located on the penultimate syllable, whereas in Type D words, it is located on the antepenultimate syllable. ... [Type B:] it is located on the penultimate syllable of the unit formed by one word and one clitic. In the absence of a clitic, the kernel of Type B words is realized on the word-final syllable

new_statements.relation_note: Same author and same analysis type as the catalog record (Yokoyama 2017 diss.: Kunigami has pitch accent with a rising kernel 上げ核 whose presence/absence and position are distinctive; catalog classification tonal). The 2026 chapter agrees on the type (lexical pitch accent realized by pitch rise, unaccented vs accented classes) and adds/updates detail: kernel position stated in syllables from the right edge (penult = Type C, antepenult = Type D, penult of word+clitic = Type B, i.e. word-final in isolation) rather than the diss.'s '1st/2nd/3rd mora from the end' (the chapter argues explicitly that the syllable, not the mora, is the counting unit, Table 13.3 p. 324); four classes A-D; domain =…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kunigami Okinoerabu has a lexical pitch accent (word-tone) system, not stress: words contrast by the presence/absence and location of a 'raising kernel' (L*+H; the syllable after the kernel-bearing syllable is high). Four lexical classes: Type A unaccented (only a non-accentual pitch rise at the end of the bunsetsu); Type B kernel on the penultimate syllable of word+first clitic (word-final, lengthened syllable when no clitic follows); Type C kernel on the penultimate syllable of the lexical word; Type D kernel on the antepenultimate syllable. Two-mora nouns show 3 patterns, three-mora nouns 4. Kernel location is computed right-to-left from the right edge; the counting unit and TBU is the syllable (mora only in a few monosyllabic heavy Type C words like naa 'inside', wui 'bucket', explained diachronically). The domain of tone assignment is argued to be the bunsetsu, with at most one kernel per bunsetsu. The system is obligatory (every word has at least one high-pitched prominence in the bunsetsu) but not culminative (Type C words of 3+ morae surface with two H's, e.g. ⸢fu⸣ta⸢bi 'this year'). In Uwano's typology it is debated whether Kunigami is multipattern or a four-pattern (N-pattern) system. The word 'stress' is not used; prominence is described entirely in terms of pitch/tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None as such (no stress). The chapter describes 'redundant' (predictable) word-initial pitch rises: in Type B all syllables before the kernel syllable are high, in Type C only the word-initial syllable is high (§3.2, p. 329); Type A has a redundant bunsetsu-final rise (§3.3, p. 330). These are non-contrastive and predictable from the kernel position.
new_statements.exceptions: Two-mora words consisting of one heavy syllable (naa 'inside', wui 'bucket') realize the kernel rise within the syllable and require the mora as counting unit/TBU; assigned to Type C and explained as reflexes of proto-Ryukyuan disyllables (*naka, *woke) (pp. 324-325). Type D is argued to be a historical split from Type C conditioned by a close vowel in the penultimate syllable, later extended to recent loans (takako, akemi, tomato, terebi) regardless of vowel height (p. 328). Compounds: A+X -> A; B+B -> B; B+A/C -> C; C+X -> C (16 compounds only, pp. 326-327).
new_statements.identity_note: All data are from the Kunigami variety (easternmost village, Eastern Okinoerabu group) of Okinoerabu, two male speakers born 1945 and 1947; the chapter notes that each of the island's 42 villages has a distinct variety and that Masana (per Matsumori 2000) distinguishes patterns by pitch FALL rather than rise, so the description should be filed under Okinoerabu, Kunigami dialect (as the catalog record already is), not generalized to all Okinoerabu varieties.

The Masana dialect has a three-pattern accent system; looking at the vocabulary belonging to each pattern (here called type a, type b, type c), one sees from the following examples that classes 3-4-5 of disyllabic nouns have split in two, giving 1-2 / 3-4-5 / 3-4-5. ... tone_statements.quote: アクセントは一種の上げ核（その位置の次を上げる核）であり，その有無と位置が弁別的である（n モーラ語に n+1 種）。通時的にはいわゆる高起群が無核で低起群は有核だが，共時的には無核語が低く始まり，有核語は，語頭核語以外は高く始まる… 通時的な高起群，低起群に属することを順に「a, b」で表わす。また，無核を「0」で表わす（従って無核語は「a0」と表わせる）。… 松森晶子（2000, 2012）の A, B, C (, D) 系列は順に a0, b1, b2 (, b3) に対応する。
tone_statements.translation: The accent is a kind of raising kernel (a kernel that raises what follows its position), and its presence/absence and position are distinctive (n+1 types for an n-mora word). Diachronically the so-called high-beginning group is kernel-less and the low-beginning group has a kernel, but synchronically kernel-less words begin low and kerneled words, except initial-kernel words, begin high... Membership in the diachronic high-/low-beginning groups is written 'a, b'; kernel-less is written '0' (so kernel-less words are 'a0')... Matsumori's (2000, 2012) classes A, B, C (, D) correspond to a0, b1, b2 (, b3).
tone_statements.locator: p. e62, §3 アクセント(1)—上げ核の性質，名詞のアクセント体系
tone_statements.summary: Rising-kernel (上げ核) pitch accent: presence and location contrastive, n+1 patterns for n-mora nouns (a0, b1-b4, Table 1); verbs 2 patterns, adjectives 3 (p.e63). No fixed tone count given.

tone_statements.quote: アクセントについては、連載後にまとめて述べる予定であるが、たとえば重起伏調はよく見られる最後から２番目だけが１拍低下するタイプではなく、[’a:]tucjiti[da[(朝日)のように、最後の「高」の前に３モーラ以上あるときは最初の２モーラだけが高くなるタイプであることが長い単語を調べることによって明らかになっている(最初の２モーラが１音節の場合、その途中で下降が現れることもあるが、その間に対立はない)。’u[ti]cjiri(穀物や食べ物の落ちこぼれ 意味は原文のまま)のような新しい型も見つかっている。
tone_statements.translation: As for the accent, I plan to discuss it comprehensively after the serialisation is complete, but, for example, by examining long words it has become clear that the double-peaked contour is not the commonly seen type in which only the second-to-last mora is lowered by one beat, but a type in which, when three or more morae precede the final 'High', only the first two morae become high, as in [’a:]tucjiti[da[ ('morning sun') (when the first two morae form one syllable a fall may appear within it, but there is no contrast there). New patterns such as ’u[ti]cjiri (…) have also been found.

tone_statements.translation: (2) The accent system of the Wadomari dialect of Okinoerabu Island (below, the isolation pattern and the pattern with particle nu are given side by side; H marks high pitch, L low pitch; the small H, L contained in LʟH, LLʜ etc. mark a pitch that appears on the latter mora of a long syllable) ... In this Wadomari dialect, of the six patterns (a)-(f) of three-syllable words, the words that appear in patterns (d), (e), (f) are limited to a very few ... First, one-syllable and three-syllable words have patterns whose fall from H to L is on the first mora (isolation Hʟ, HLL; with particle HʟL, HLLL), whereas two-syllable words lack the corresponding pattern.

tone_statements.translation: I take up the conjugated forms of the Okinoerabu dialects of the Amami Islands and present accent data for them. For the dialects of this island I have already treated the basic forms of verbs/adjectives in 23 settlements (Uwano 1998) and the nominals of 35 settlements (Uwano 1999). This paper continues those and forms a unit with them. The analysis is left to a separate paper.

tone_statements.quote: Accent is phonemic and is a matter of pitch as it is throughout Japan wherever accent is phonemic. The phonemics of accent can here be adequately described in terms of two levels of pitch, although phonetically more levels can be distinguished by the ear. The mora is the unit used to describe accent. Each word has a fixed pattern of high and low pitches. ... Words with a sharp drop in pitch within or just after the word are said to have accent and are marked with a ⌉ at the point where the drop in pitch occurs. ... For both two and three mora words there are three accent types.
tone_statements.summary: Phonemic pitch accent: accentless vs. accented words (locus of pitch fall), two pitch levels, mora-based; 3 accent types for 2-3-mora nouns; verb/adjective accent tables. Hattori accent word list.

sources.quote: 3.3 節では、アクセントの体系について論じる。国頭方言は、音の相対的な高低によって語を弁別するピッチ・アクセント (pitch accent) を持つ。... 国頭方言のアクセント核はもっぱらピッチ上昇によって実現される。... 本節では、高山（2013）にならい、国頭方言は上げ核の有無と位置が弁別的な体系であると考える。 3.3.1. 概論 前述のように、国頭方言は核の有無と位置が弁別的である体系を持つ。すなわち、国頭方言の語は、核を持つもの（hagami「鏡」、futabi「今年」、guzjija「鯨」など）と持たないもの（hjibusji「煙」など）とに分類することが可能である。... 国頭方言における核の位置は、後ろから 1 モーラ目、後ろから 2 モーラ目、後ろから 3 モーラ目のいずれかである。したがって核の有無（あるかないか）と位置（後ろから 1 番目か 2 番目か 3 番目か）とに基づいて、4 種類のアクセント型が区別される。以下、国頭方言の 4 種類のアクセント型をそれぞれ a 型、b 型、c 型、d 型と呼ぶことにする。a 型は核のない型、すなわち無核であり、b 型、c 型、d 型は核のある型、すなわち有核である。... [§3.3.3] a. 核を担う韻律単位はモーラである。b. a 型は核のない型であり、b 型は後ろから 1 モーラ目に、c 型は後ろから 2 モーラ目に、d 型は後ろから 3 モーラ目に核がある型である。ただし b 型は 2 モーラ以上の助詞が後接するとき、核の位置が 1 モーラ右側に移る。c. 核は上げ核であり、核があるモーラの次の韻律単位を上昇させる。

sources.quote: These studies have argued that the tonal patterns of Kunigami are lexically contrastive (see §2.6), with distinctions made based on the presence or absence of a raising accent kernel (see §2.3 of Chapter 1, this volume) and, when present, its location within the word. Words lacking a kernel are unaccented (Type A), whereas words with a kernel are accented. ... In Type C words, the kernel is located on the penultimate syllable, whereas in Type D words, it is located on the antepenultimate syllable. ... [Type B:] it is located on the penultimate syllable of the unit formed by one word and one clitic. In the absence of a clitic, the kernel of Type B words is realized on the word-final syllable

sources.quote: Accent is phonemic and is a matter of pitch as it is throughout Japan wherever accent is phonemic. For both two and three mora words there are three accent types.

tone.translation: As for the accent, I plan to discuss it comprehensively after the serialisation is complete, but, for example, by examining long words it has become clear that the double-peaked contour is not the commonly seen type in which only the second-to-last mora is lowered by one beat, but a type in which, when three or more morae precede the final 'High', only the first two morae become high, as in [’a:]tucjiti[da[ ('morning sun') (when the first two morae form one syllable a fall may appear within it, but there is no contrast there).
